Ableton/Live/v/12/Note Probability Group — Turn familiar per-note Chance into a shared decision for a chord, a drum fill, or a choice of pitches.
Ableton/Live/v/12/MIDI Tools — Generate notes and reshape them directly in a clip. Try Seed, then use Follow Actions if the next phrase should depend on the current one.

Keys and scales — Choose a root and scale in the Control Bar or clip properties, then enable Scale Mode. Highlight or fold the piano roll to the scale while writing; compatible devices and MIDI tools can follow the clip's scale. Ableton/Live/UG/10 Editing MIDI/06 Folding and Scales

Tuning systems — Load a Scala tuning from the Browser to explore pitches outside twelve-tone equal temperament. Live's instruments follow it; check plug-in and hardware support before relying on external instruments to match. Ableton/Live/UG/15 Tuning Systems
Find sounds and work in Arrangement

Browser tags — Select a Browser category and use Filter View to narrow sounds by descriptive tags across content types. Add your own tags to make sounds easier to find later. Ableton/Live/UG/04 Browser/04 Filters and Tags

Arrangement mixer — Open Mixer using the view control at the bottom right or Cmd+Option+M on Mac. Mix levels and sends while the Arrangement stays visible; Session and Arrangement mixer visibility can be set independently. Ableton's view options FAQ
Find sounds and work in Arrangement
Stacked Detail Views — Show the Clip View and Device View together to edit a clip while adjusting its devices. Ableton's Live 12 feature guide
Find sounds and work in Arrangement

Bounce — Select a clip or time range and choose Bounce to New Track to print its devices to audio; Live mutes the source selection. The bounce is pre-mixer, so volume, pan and sends remain mixer settings. Bounce Track in Place replaces the earlier Freeze and Flatten command. Ableton/Live/UG/20 Bounce to Audio/01 Bouncing Individual Tracks

Stem Separation — In Live 12.3 Suite and later, right-click an audio clip and choose Separate Stems to New Audio Tracks to isolate vocals, drums, bass or other sounds. Live 12.4 can process a selected Arrangement time range. Ableton/Live/UG/22 Stem Separation/02 Separating Audio Files and Clips

Link Audio — Live 12.4 can stream audio between compatible Link Audio peers on the same network. Enable Link Audio in the Link menu, then route audio between peers. Original Link synchronizes timing; Link Audio also carries audio. Ableton's Link Audio FAQ

New and updated devices — Try Ableton/Live/UG/29 Audio Effect Reference/33 Roar for multistage saturation, or Auto Shift for pitch correction on monophonic audio. Live 12.4 also updates Erosion and other devices; older Sets retain Erosion Legacy. Live 12 release notes
Ableton/Live/UG has the reference by chapter. Compare Live editions shows which tools and devices come with each edition.

Live 11 could send MIDI CC through clip envelopes, and Max for Live devices could expose custom dials. Live 12 adds CC Control, a stock MIDI effect with named dials for automation or live control. Ableton made it available in all editions with 12.0.5. Ableton's guide to sending MIDI CC · Live 12 release notes

Enable Track on the MicroFreak's MIDI output port in Live's MIDI settings. On a MIDI track, set MIDI To to the MicroFreak port and match its receive channel. Monitor the synth's audio through your interface or directly from the hardware. Ableton's MIDI routing reference

Drop CC Control on that MIDI track. Set a Custom B–M dial's CC Type to CC 23 and name it Cutoff. Play a sustained note and turn the dial to hear the filter move. Arturia's MicroFreak MIDI implementation chart

Show automation in Arrangement View and draw a sweep for the Cutoff dial. To play it by hand, map an incoming controller to the dial using Live's MIDI Map Mode and enable Remote for that controller's input. The incoming mapping controls the dial in Live, and the dial sends CC 23 to the synth. Ableton's MIDI mapping reference
Ableton/Live/UG/30 MIDI Effect Reference/02 CC Control explains the custom controls, Learn, and Send.

Live 12 adds Generate and Transform to the MIDI clip editor. A Generator creates notes in the clip. A Transformation reshapes the clip's existing notes. Once applied, the result is editable piano-roll material. Ableton/Live/UG/11 MIDI Tools describes the clip tools and their controls.

In an empty looping MIDI clip, open Generate and select Seed. Choose a narrow pitch range, set Voices to one, and adjust Density, Duration, and Velocity. Turn off Auto Apply to adjust the controls before pressing Apply.

Keep a phrase you like, then select its notes and try Transform → Ornament to add grace notes. Play the loop to hear the edited notes. For variation during playback, try Ableton/Live/v/12/Note Probability Group on some of those notes.

Ableton/Live/UG/11 MIDI Tools/03 Generative Tools/02 Seed covers the range controls. Seed draws notes within those constraints and offers no control for the probability of the next pitch given the preceding pitch.
Make the next phrase depend on the current one

In Session View, put three phrase clips named A, B, and C in consecutive slots on one track. On each clip, enable Follow Actions and set Linked with one play-through. Turn on the global Follow Actions switch.
Make the next phrase depend on the current one

Give clip A two Jump targets, B at 80% and C at 20%. Give clip B two Jump targets, A at 60% and C at 40%. In clip C, use Jump to B at 90% and Play Again at 10%. Jump targets use scene numbers. Launch any clip and listen as the currently playing phrase determines the next set of odds. Launch another clip manually to pick a new current phrase.
Make the next phrase depend on the current one

Follow Actions already work in Live 11. Each clip supplies the transition probabilities for a first-order Markov chain whose states are phrases. Ableton/Live/Action/Follow covers the controls, and Ableton's Live 11 Follow Actions guide explains Jump and Linked timing.
Make the next phrase depend on the current one

For note-level transitions, Metrosync's gtm.markov transform is a third-party Max for Live Transformation for monophonic melodies. Its second-order model uses the previous two states. Install the prebuilt tool from the gtm.markov Max package and open it in the MIDI clip's Transform tab.

Live 11's Chance lane gives each note its own probability. Live 12 can share a Chance value across selected notes. Play All makes a chord or fill happen together. Play One picks a single note at random when the group plays. Live 11 Chance Editor · Live 12 Probability Groups
Try a chord, then a choice of pitches

Put a chord on the last beat of a looping MIDI clip. Select its notes and choose Group Notes (Play All) from the MIDI Note Editor context menu. Open the Chance lane and set the diamond marker to 50%. Listen for the whole chord or silence at that beat.
Try a chord, then a choice of pitches

Switch the group to Play One and set its triangle marker to 100%. Each pass plays one of the pitches at that beat. Lowering the group Chance changes how often a note sounds. Live exposes one group Chance value and chooses the member at random, so the group has no per-member weighting control.
Try a chord, then a choice of pitches
